body:
Two compounding problems:

(1) No client-side validation of price input. ItemFormViewModel accepts any
string; the server validates amount against ^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$ and 422s. A
European user typing "1,99" (decimal comma) — or "2€", "1.999" — creates a
dirty row the server will always reject. Server-side apply_changes runs in one
transaction, so the 422 aborts the WHOLE sync request: pushes AND pulls both
stop working, permanently, for every list. SyncWorker maps Failed -> retry(),
so WorkManager re-sends the same doomed payload on backoff forever.

(2) Nothing surfaces sync state. No screen shows last-synced time, pending
changes, or errors — the app just silently stops reflecting other devices.

Fix, layered:
- ItemFormViewModel: validate + normalize price at input/save time (accept
  comma decimal -> dot; strip currency symbols/whitespace; reject >2 decimals
  with an inline error). Same for currency (3-letter code or blank; settings
  screen already does this — item form doesn't).
- Surface sync health: minimal viable = a quiet "last synced / N changes
  pending / sync failing" line (e.g. overview or drawer), loud when the same
  failure repeats.
- Defense in depth (server, small): include the offending row id + field in
  the 422 error envelope so a client can quarantine that row (clear its dirty
  bit / flag it for user attention) instead of blocking the queue forever.
  Wire-contract addition, backward compatible (extra JSON keys).

Files: android ui/item/ItemFormViewModel.kt, data/sync/SyncEngine.kt +
SyncWorker.kt, a small UI surface; server sync.py validation errors.
Related: server tests for the enriched 422 envelope.
title: Android: one invalid field wedges sync forever, and sync failures are invisible
